title_vi: Kẻ điên: Những ngụ ngôn và bài thơ
translation_direction: en → vi; direct from the specifically identified complete English electronic witness
ai_disclosure: Direct AI-produced Vietnamese prose by Claude Opus 5.5. The drafting system conducted the final full assessment; a separate-context assessment by the same model family read every pair and supplied findings first. No human translator, editor, reviewer, independent model consensus or actual reader feedback is recorded.

entry_conditions: Complete named-source and Vietnamese texts, explicit alignment and exact content hashes.
Compare every source and target passage; disclose that this assessor also revised the text and has seen earlier AI assessments.
Source and target edition titles are present and compared explicitly; the title review must match both catalog title strings exactly.
exit_conditions: One complete AI review with a weighted score at least 8.6 using the five unchanged weights and half-point category scores; no separate numerical dimension floors.
All canonical passages reviewed; no unresolved major or critical finding; source and target hashes match the final text.
Publication and rights status are recorded separately in the edition catalog; an AI score does not supply a license.
The selected review includes source_title, target_title and a substantive title rationale; changed titles require a fresh matching review.
review_process.human_feedback: Optional after publication or while a work remains a draft; no prior human publication review is required by v2.

decisions.decision: Gibran’s solemn, simple parabolic voice is rendered in short, clean sentences with his repetitions kept identical; the piece titles are short Vietnamese titles.
decisions.rationale: The parables depend on rhythm and repetition more than on vocabulary.

decisions.decision: The Gospel quotation inside ‘The Blessed City’ (Matthew 5:29–30) is translated close to the standard Vietnamese biblical sense and kept as its own unit, which a first extraction had dropped.
decisions.rationale: The corpus must hold every sentence of the witness.

revision_history.scope: Complete initial direct translation, separate-context full source/target assessment and concrete revisions before the selected final review.

changes.explanation: Optatives rendered as indicatives (units 6 and 110), ‘comrade’ as ‘đồng chí’ (unit 24) and pronoun/register slips in the first prologue pieces were corrected.
The Defeat refrain’s pronoun, ‘in child-bed’ and ‘how large a foot-print’ were corrected and the refrain made identical.
Pronoun and gender inconsistencies for the blade of grass (units 236–238) and the body-part names (241–245) were unified.
The Gospel quotation, missing from the first extraction, was added and its wording smoothed.

selection_limit: Chosen for a complete, directly sourced and openly reusable Vietnamese edition. Existing Vietnamese translations, their quality and reader demand have not been comprehensively assessed; no absence or superiority claim is made.

glossary.rationale: The speaker of the prologue and the book’s title figure; one pair of terms throughout.

glossary.draft_rendering: Thượng Đế / Đấng Chủ Tể / Đấng Tạo Hóa / Cha
glossary.rationale: The four prayers of the first piece use one rising series of addresses.

glossary.draft_rendering: Thất bại, Thất bại của tôi
glossary.rationale: The refrain stays identical on every repetition and the speaker is ‘tôi’ throughout.

glossary.draft_rendering: ngươi, hỡi — a formal, solemn but plain address
glossary.rationale: Gibran’s King-James tint is given a formal Vietnamese equivalent without obscure archaisms.

witness_decision: Selected Project Gutenberg #5616, an electronic transcription of Kahlil Gibran’s The Madman (New York: Alfred A. Knopf, 1918). The page does not name the printing and the text was not collated with the 1918 edition.

unresolved_questions.explanation: The King James tint of Gibran’s English is only partly carried; the prayers open with ‘Hỡi’ but the rest is plain modern Vietnamese.

title_review.source_title: The Madman: His Parables and Poems
title_review.target_title: Kẻ điên: Những ngụ ngôn và bài thơ
title_review.rationale: The Vietnamese title ‘Kẻ điên: Những ngụ ngôn và bài thơ’ is this edition’s own rendering; no earlier Vietnamese title was checked.

passage_assessment_notes.assessment: The prologue: how I became a madman.
